title: Geo strategy
summary: How to pick, price and adapt to countries, with a close look at Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Cameroon. You learn the economics of a geo, how to localise honestly and how to expand one market at a time while respecting local rules.

lessons.title: Geo tiers and the economics of a geo
objectives: By the end you can explain what Tier 1, 2 and 3 usually mean and why lists differ.
You can compare two geos on cost per FTD, margin, ROI and daily volume.
You can list the non-price factors that decide whether a geo works.

steps.h: Every country is a different market
steps.p: A campaign that works in one country can fail next door. Prices, payouts, languages, payment habits and laws all change at the border. Geo strategy means choosing where to run, adapting to each place and expanding in a planned order.

d.b: Each geo is its own market

steps.say: Let's start with a simple idea. Every country is its own market. A campaign that works well in one country can fail in the country next door. Prices, payouts, languages, payment habits and laws all change at the border. That's why geo strategy matters. It means choosing where to run, adapting to each place, and expanding in a planned order. Same offer, different economics.

steps.p: Networks and buyers often group countries into tiers. Tier 1 usually means high-income markets with expensive traffic and high payouts. Tier 3 means cheaper traffic and lower payouts. There is no official list, and every network draws the lines a little differently.
d: Tier 1|expensive traffic, high payouts, heavy competition
Tier 3|cheap traffic, lower payouts, big audiences
Your list|what your network actually pays
steps.say: Networks and buyers often group countries into tiers. Look at the cards. Tier one usually means high-income markets, with expensive traffic, high payouts and heavy competition. Tier two sits in the middle. Tier three means cheaper traffic, lower payouts and big audiences. But here's the catch: there's no official list, and every network draws the lines a little differently. That's why the last card matters most. Your list is what your network actually pays.

steps.h: Cheap traffic can still lose money
steps.p: Cheap clicks are tempting, but a geo is profitable only when the payout covers cost per action with a margin. A low-cost geo with low payouts and weak conversion can lose money, while an expensive geo can be profitable when the payout is high enough.
steps.say: Cheap clicks are tempting. But a geo is only profitable when the payout covers your cost per action, with a margin left over. Compare the two columns. The lower-cost geo gives you cheap C P M, that's cost per thousand impressions, and more reach per dollar, but lower payouts, and payment habits may limit deposits. The higher-cost geo has expensive clicks and strong competition, but higher payouts. So an expensive geo can still be the profitable one.

steps.p: Every geo comes down to one comparison. Work out what one result costs you there and compare it with what that result pays. The formula is the same everywhere. Only the inputs change from country to country.
steps.say: Every geo comes down to one comparison. Look at the formula on screen. Payout, minus cost per F T D, that's cost per first time deposit, equals your margin per F T D. Work out what one result costs you there, then compare it with what that result pays. The formula is the same in every country. Only the inputs change.

steps.h: Example: two geos side by side
steps.p: Example numbers only. Geo A has expensive traffic and a high payout. Geo B has cheap traffic and a low payout. Work down each column from CPM to margin, and compare what each FTD leaves you with after its cost.
steps.more: Check Geo A: 1,000 impressions cost $8 and bring 15 clicks, so CPC is $8 ÷ 15 ≈ $0.53. At 1% click to FTD you need 100 clicks per FTD, so cost per FTD ≈ $53. Margin is $150 − $53 = $97. Geo B: 1,000 impressions cost $1.50 and bring 20 clicks, so CPC is $0.075. At 0.5% you need 200 clicks per FTD, so cost per FTD is $15. Margin is $35 − $15 = $20.
steps.say: Here are example numbers only. Geo A has expensive traffic and a high payout. Geo B has cheap traffic and a low payout. Work down each column. Geo A costs eight dollars per thousand impressions, gets fifteen clicks, so about fifty three cents a click. At one percent click to F T D, that's about fifty three dollars per F T D, against a hundred and fifty dollar payout, leaving about ninety seven dollars. Geo B ends at fifteen dollars per F T D against thirty five, leaving twenty.

steps.p: Geo A earns more per FTD, but ROI shows return per dollar spent. Example: Geo A returns about 181% and Geo B about 133%. Then check volume, because a geo that only takes $50 a day may matter less than one that takes $500.
steps.more: ROI is margin divided by cost. Geo A: $96.67 ÷ $53.33 ≈ 1.81, so about 181% when worked from unrounded figures. Geo B: $20 ÷ $15 ≈ 1.33, so 133%. Both are healthy in this example. The next question is how much each geo can absorb before cost per FTD starts to rise.
steps.say: Geo A earns more per F T D. But R O I, return on investment, shows return per dollar spent. It's margin divided by cost. Look at the bars. In this example, Geo A returns about one hundred and eighty one percent, and Geo B about one hundred and thirty three percent. Both are healthy. Then check volume, because a geo that only takes fifty dollars a day may matter less than one that takes five hundred.

steps.h: Lab: the most you can pay in Geo B
steps.p: Before you test a geo, work out the most you can pay per FTD and still keep your margin. Example: Geo B pays $35 per FTD and you want to keep 25%. Enter the maximum cost per FTD, which becomes your target CPA there.
steps.more: Answer: $26.25. $35 × (1 − 0.25) = $26.25. That is your target in Geo B. Break-even is $35, and the CPA kill line is the lower of 1.5 × target ($39.38) and break-even, so $35. In the example, Geo B's $15 cost per FTD sits far under target.

That number becomes your target C P A, cost per acquisition, in that geo. Pause and try it, then check your answer.

steps.h: Daily spend you can actually place
steps.p: Profit depends on ROI and on how much you can spend at that ROI. A geo where you can place $300 a day near target can earn more in total than one that only takes $40, even with a lower ROI.
steps.more: Example: Geo B at $300 a day and 133% ROI makes about $400 profit a day. Geo A at $40 a day and 181% ROI makes about $72 a day. Daily capacity depends on audience size, how fast creatives fatigue, offer caps and competition. You only learn it by scaling carefully and watching cost per FTD.

steps.h: What changes from geo to geo
steps.p: Beyond prices, these factors decide whether an offer works in a country. Check each one before launch, because one weak link, such as no local payment method, can break a funnel that looks good on paper.
d: Devices and data|phones, speed, data cost
steps.say: Beyond prices, these factors decide whether an offer works in a country. Look at the six cards: language, payments, devices and data, timing, rules, and trust. Check each one before launch. Why? Because one weak link, like no local payment method, can break a funnel that looks good on paper. Your numbers can be perfect and still fail if people can't deposit the way they're used to.

steps.h: Tier labels go out of date
steps.p: Tier labels are a starting point. Costs and payouts change with seasons, competition and regulation, and a geo that was cheap last year may be crowded now. Use your own recent numbers and recheck before you plan a budget.

d.text: Never assume a payout or CPM from a forum post or an old offer sheet. Get current terms from your network and test with a small budget.

steps.p: Most bad geo choices come from looking at one number. These mistakes each focus on something real, such as cheap clicks or a high payout, while ignoring the factor that actually decides profit.
d: Chasing cheap CPM|payout and conversion decide profit
Chasing high payouts|traffic may cost more than it pays
Ignoring caps|a 10-a-day cap limits total profit
Assuming payment methods|check the deposit page yourself
Trusting old payout sheets|get current terms in writing
steps.say: Most bad geo choices come from looking at one number. Look at these cards. Chasing cheap C P M ignores that payout and conversion decide profit. Chasing high payouts ignores that traffic may cost more than it pays. Ignoring caps forgets that a ten a day cap limits total profit. Assuming payment methods, instead of checking the deposit page yourself. And trusting old payout sheets instead of current terms in writing.

lessons.title: West Africa: Nigeria and Ghana
objectives: By the end you can describe the main languages, currencies, payment habits and time zones of Nigeria and Ghana.
You can adapt a funnel to local payment habits and light mobile pages.
You can list what to check on regulation before running in either country.

steps.p: Nigeria and Ghana share English as the main language of business and ads, a strong mobile culture and plenty of shared music and humour. They still differ in currency, payment habits, regulators and time zone, so treat them as separate geos with separate campaigns.

d.s: Own campaign, budget and sheet for each

steps.say: Nigeria and Ghana have a lot in common. English is the main language of business and ads, both have a strong mobile culture, and they share plenty of music and humour. But they still differ in currency, payment habits, regulators and time zone. So treat them as separate geos. Each one gets its own campaign, its own budget and its own sheet.

steps.p: Nigeria is a large and varied market. Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt behave differently from smaller cities, and the north differs from the south. Treat these points as general starting notes and confirm them with your own data.
d: Language|English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo and more
Payments|bank transfer, cards, USSD, fintech apps
steps.say: Here's Nigeria at a glance. Languages include English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo and more. The currency is the naira. Payments run through bank transfer, cards, U S S D and fintech apps. The time zone is West Africa Time, U T C plus one. It's a large and varied market. Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt behave differently from smaller cities, and the north differs from the south. Treat these as starting notes, and confirm them with your own data.

steps.p: Ghana is smaller than Nigeria, with a different rhythm and its own regulators. Mobile money is part of daily life for many people. As with every geo in this module, use these as starting notes and check them against your data.
d: Language|English, Twi and other local languages
steps.say: Now Ghana. The languages include English, Twi and other local languages. The currency is the cedi. For payments, mobile money is part of daily life for many people, alongside bank transfer and cards. The time zone is G M T, U T C plus zero. Ghana is smaller than Nigeria, with a different rhythm and its own regulators. Again, use these as starting notes and check them against your data.

steps.p: If depositing feels hard, people drop off at the last step. In Nigeria, many people are used to instant bank transfers and fintech apps. In Ghana, mobile money wallets are an everyday habit for many. Check the offer supports what your audience actually uses.
steps.say: If depositing feels hard, people drop off at the last step. Compare the two checklists. In Nigeria, many people are used to instant bank transfers and fintech apps, so check that local transfers and naira deposits work. In Ghana, mobile money wallets are an everyday habit for many, so check mobile money and cedi deposits, and explain the wallet steps simply. In both, show the minimum deposit in local currency.

steps.p: Language choice is about comfort. Many Nigerians switch between English and Pidgin naturally, and a friendly Pidgin line can feel more personal. Keep it respectful, keep claims honest and make sure the offer page itself is clear.

steps.p: Use faces, places and references people recognise. A Lagos street scene feels different from Accra, and viewers notice. Never use fake testimonials, and never use logos, celebrities or news brands without permission.

steps.p: Both countries regulate gambling and financial promotions, and the bodies and rules involved can change. In Nigeria, gaming oversight involves national and state-level bodies. Do not rely on old forum posts. Check current law and the ad platform's rules before you run.

steps.say: Both countries regulate gambling and financial promotions, and the bodies and rules involved can change. In Nigeria, gaming oversight involves national and state-level bodies. Run through this checklist: is the offer licensed for this country, is platform authorization needed, what are the age limits, which risk warnings are required in the ad and lander, and what are the rules on earnings claims. Don't rely on old forum posts. Check current law and the platform's rules.

steps.p: Translating words is the smallest part of localising. People respond to faces, places, money, humour and payment steps they recognise. A localised campaign feels like it was made for them. A translated one often feels like it was made somewhere else.

steps.p: Cameroon is a useful case because it is officially bilingual. Most of the country is French-speaking, with English-speaking regions in the west. Pidgin and Camfranglais are also heard in daily life. Treat these as general notes and confirm with local people.
